title: ActivitySpec
description: Doc §3.2. This is the frozen contract for activity_version.spec_jsonb — changes require joint PR approval per PLAN.md 'conflict-minimizing rules'. Authored as YAML in Git (content-as-code, D4), projected into this JSON Schema for CI lint (§3.5 step 1) and Postgres JSONB storage.

cloud.description: Phase 3 (memory.md §5.3). CLOUD_ACCOUNT-tier only. `regions` is the allow-list the SCP framework grants for this activity's vended account (empty ⇒ the org default two regions). `sku_exceptions` lists otherwise-SCP-denied instance classes / services this blueprint legitimately needs (e.g. a GPU family for an ML project) — the Account Pool Manager writes these onto an account tag at claim time and the expensive-SKU SCP is conditioned on that tag. Adding an entry here is a security-review checkpoint (PLAN_PHASE3_PROJECTS.md A2).

milestones.description: Phase 3 (PLAN.md 169, memory.md §12.3). PROJECT-mode only — the ordered gate sequence design→infra→implementation→hardening→final. Each milestone declares which of the activity's `tasks` (by key) it gates, an optional AI rubric slice, whether it needs a T3 environment provisioned, and its gate rule. `gate` = ALL_VALIDATORS_PASS (deterministic gate), RUBRIC_MIN_LEVEL (must reach `min_level`/5 on `rubric`), or BOTH. A hard-gated milestone (`blocking: true`) blocks the next milestone until it passes — memory.md §12.3: 'three weeks of implementation on a bad design teaches the wrong lesson and burns real cloud budget.' Absent on GUIDED_LAB / PRODUCTION_SIM.

blocking.description: true ⇒ the next milestone is LOCKED until this one reaches GATED_PASS

environment_required.description: false for `design` (near-zero cost, no T3 account claimed); true for infra/implementation/hardening/final

task_keys.description: keys into this spec's `tasks[]` array that this milestone's :submit runs and gates on

rubric.description: rubric id (content/rubrics/<id>.yaml) — required when gate is RUBRIC_MIN_LEVEL or BOTH, e.g. rub.architecture.v3 for `design`

min_level.description: required when gate is RUBRIC_MIN_LEVEL or BOTH — the floor on the rubric's 1–5 scale (memory.md §12.3: design gate is level 3/5)

defence.description: Phase 3 (PLAN.md 173, memory.md §12.3). PROJECT-mode only — the milestone-5 viva. The question generator reads the learner's OWN milestone-1 design artifact and OWN commit history and produces `num_questions` grounded questions; the transcript is scored against `rubric` (rub.reasoning.v1) and human-reviewed for certification. Calls the model directly (not Phase 4's Mentor Service).

health_gate.description: Doc §3.2/§7.3 worked example: checks that MUST pass before any fault in `faults` is applied. Phase 1's actual gate is still just 'pod reached Ready' (orchestrator's WaitForPodReady, doc §5.5 step 4) -- this field lets content declare a richer PRODUCTION_SIM-specific gate for a later health-gate implementation to read, without blocking fault-injection wiring on that richer gate existing yet.

faults.description: Doc §3.2/§7.3 worked example, PLAN.md Phase 2 integration point: PRODUCTION_SIM's fault manifest, applied after the health gate passes. apply_at 'T0' means immediately after health gate; 'T+<seconds>' means that many seconds after T0, for escalation sequences -- the T+ scheduling itself is a later increment (see AttemptService.provision()'s doc comment), T0 is what Phase 2's initial wiring actually executes.

process_signals.description: Doc §3.3 worked example. blast_radius.forbidden is a list of command substrings the Session Broker's telemetry tap checks every COMMAND_EXECUTED against (orchestrator/internal/sessionbroker/telemetry_tap.go) -- 'a learner who fixes the 502 by deleting the namespace... should not score well.' diagnostic_efficiency's good/bad action lists are the raw material for the diagnostic_efficiency criterion (fn.diagnostic_efficiency.v1) -- both are PRODUCTION_SIM-only signals, absent on GUIDED_LAB activities.

artifacts_required.description: Doc §3.3 worked example / §6.5: written artifacts the learner must submit (e.g. an incident note), graded against a rubric. ArtifactService.gradeArtifact reads rubric by id from content/rubrics/<rubric>.yaml (RubricRepository -- no rubric/rubric_version table exists, same content-as-code pattern as content/faults).

validators.description: §3.5 CI lint step 1: every task must have >=1 validator

on_fail.description: required field per §3.2 design notes: generic failure text is the #1 cause of lab abandonment

config.description: Phase 3 (memory.md §6.2, §12.3). Per-type execution config for the T3 validator executors. Which sub-object applies is keyed off the sibling `type`. All optional so a minimal test spec need not fabricate one; the executor validates the shape it needs at run time and returns ERROR (never a learner-scored FAIL) if required config is absent.

iac_state.description: IAC_STATE — Terraform state checks. `working_dir` is the repo-relative dir to run `terraform` in; `no_drift` runs `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` and fails on exit 2; `require_remote_backend` fails if the backend is `local`; `forbid_secrets_in_state` scans the pulled state for high-entropy / known-key patterns.

cloud_assert.description: CLOUD_ASSERT — read-only cloud topology assertions run with a validator-scoped STS role (MintValidatorCredentials, scope cloud.read_only). `checks` is an ordered list of named assertions the executor knows how to evaluate (e.g. no_public_data_stores, encryption_at_rest, least_privilege_iam, vpc_has_private_subnets). `params` passes check-specific arguments.

test_suite.description: TEST_SUITE — run the repo's own test command inside the T3 workspace and parse structured output. `command` is run via /bin/bash -c; `report_format` selects the parser; `report_path` is where the report lands; `min_pass_rate` (0–1) is the floor.

static_analysis.description: STATIC_ANALYSIS — tfsec / checkov / trivy with authored thresholds. `tool` picks the scanner; `target` is the repo-relative path scanned; `max_severity_allowed` is the highest finding severity that still passes; `max_findings` caps count regardless of severity.

chaos_probe.description: CHAOS_PROBE — inject a failure into the learner's deployed system and assert it survives. `action` is the disturbance (reuses the InjectFault mechanism where it maps cleanly); `target_selector` scopes it; `health_check` is the HTTP probe that must stay green throughout; `recovery_timeout_ms` is how long the service has to re-stabilise.

perf_bench.description: PERF_BENCH — drive load (k6) at the deployed system and assert a latency / throughput target. `script` is the repo-relative k6 script or an inline `target_url` + `rps`; `duration_s` is the run length; `p95_ms_max` / `error_rate_max` are the thresholds.

solution_apply.description: path to idempotent script that forces post-task state, §1.3.1
